question: How many general electoral rolls are there for every territorial constituency for election of the Parliament?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **Representation of the People Act, 1950**, there is **one general electoral roll** for each territorial constituency for the election of Parliament and State Legislatures in India.
 
• This means that all eligible voters are included in a **single list** for each constituency.
 
• The electoral roll is a comprehensive list that includes the **names of all eligible voters** within a specific territorial constituency.
 
• Maintaining a single electoral roll ensures **uniformity and accuracy** in the election process.
 
• The preparation and maintenance of the electoral rolls are overseen by the **Election Commission of India**.
 
• The process involves **periodic updates** to include new voters and remove those who are no longer eligible.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Representation of the People Act, 1950**

 
 
• The Act provides the procedure for the preparation of electoral rolls for the elections to the House of the People and the Legislative Assemblies.
 
• It also specifies the qualifications and disqualifications for registration in an electoral roll.
 
• The Act ensures that the electoral process is conducted in a fair and orderly manner.
 
 
 
• **Election Commission of India**
 
 
• The Election Commission of India is an autonomous constitutional authority responsible for administering election processes in India at national and state levels.
 
• The body administers elections to the Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, and State Legislative Assemblies, as well as the offices of the President and Vice President in the country.
